_README: Switches for design decisions that are still open (CLAUDE.md section 9).
This file is written by hand. Unlike the rest of data/, it is NOT
generated from the workbook, so export_data.py never overwrites it.
Change a 'value' below and the game behaves differently on the next run.
No code changes needed. The 'options' line lists what each flag accepts;
anything else is rejected with a readable error at startup.

default_intent_pattern.question: What should an opponent do on their turn when nobody has written a pattern for them yet?

means._: A pattern is a list of moves that repeats. A move is a verb and either one number or a range to roll between, inclusive at both ends. A move that comes out at zero is not taken: the opponent steps to the next move and does that instead, so nobody spends a turn guarding nothing.
means.attack: Lowers the player's support, minus whatever guard the player is holding.
means.block: The opponent gains guard, softening the player's next attack.

note: This is the fallback, not anybody's character. An opponent with their own
Intent pattern always uses that instead, and every opponent the six levels
put in front of the player now has one.
Pattern 1 of Cameron's five, chosen by him on 2026-09-21 as the neutral
default: the most middle-of-the-road of the set, and far gentler than the
attack 6 / gain 4 / block 5 it replaces. That one averaged a flat 6 every
third turn and measured LV01's committee as unwinnable, 0 wins in 20

turn_limit_outcome.question: If the turn limit runs out and neither side has reached the threshold, what happens?

means.loss: The player loses. Harshest, and the clearest to read.
means.highest_support_wins: Whoever is ahead on the bar wins.
means.tie_retry: The stage is replayed from the start.

opponent_can_win_by_threshold.question: Can the opponent win outright by pushing its own support past the threshold, or only by running out your clock or filling your gaffe meter?

means.false: The opponent can only win on the clock or the gaffe meter.
means.true: The opponent also wins the moment its support reaches the threshold.

opponent_engine.question: Do opponents follow a fixed, readable script, or play from a real deck?

means.intent_patterns: A fixed repeating list of moves, shown to the player a turn ahead. Recommended for the first playable version.
means.deck_ai: The opponent draws and plays its own cards. Not built yet — selecting this will stop battles from starting.

press_answer_timer.question: Do press conference questions have a countdown to answer?

means.false: No timer. The player takes as long as they like.
means.true: A countdown per question. The number of seconds comes from the Balance tab.

discard_hand_end_of_turn.question: At the end of a turn, does the player discard whatever is left in hand?

means.true: Discard the rest of the hand and draw a fresh one. Standard for this kind of game.
means.false: Unplayed cards stay in hand and the player tops up to the hand size.

pass_energy_penalty.question: What does it cost to end a turn having played nothing at all?

means.0: Passing is free. Keeping quiet and letting the clock run becomes a real tactic, which is why this is not the default.
means.1: One energy off next turn. In a caucus, where energy is a pool that is never refilled, it comes off what is left of the pool instead - the only version that means anything there. In a press conference, passing is also how you decline the question in front of you.
means.2: Two energy. Harsh on a three-energy turn: passing would cost you most of a turn on top of the turn you already gave up.

open_card_collection.question: Does a new run start owning every card in the workbook, or just the opening tier?

means.true: PLAYTEST SETTING. Every card is owned from the first moment, so a session can try the whole slate without earning it — Cameron asked for the XP and card economy to be left aside while he prices xp_to_unlock by playing. Used to be a hardcoded constant (GameState.open_collection); moved here 2026-09-22 so it is a switch like every other open decision, not a line only a programmer can flip.
means.false: A new run starts owning only the opening tier (Ledger.OPENING_TIER). Every other card must be unlocked with XP, at the cost in cards.json's xp_to_unlock column — which is null on all 54 cards today, so nothing costs anything until Cameron fills that column in.

level_gating_enabled.question: Do levels.json's own cooldown and unlock_cost_* columns actually gate which levels the Office will let you play?

means.false: Every level stays open, regardless of cooldown or unlock cost — today's behaviour. The costs and cooldowns are still shown, as information, so they are not invented later.
means.true: A level whose relevant unlock_cost_* is more than 0 must be bought with XP before it can be played (GameState.levels_unlocked / Ledger.level_unlock_cost), and a level just finished stays on cooldown for its own cooldown value's worth of OTHER level completions (GameState.levels_completed_count / level_last_completed_at) before it can be played again.

guard_cap.question: How much Guard can either side be holding at once?

means.3: Tight. Guarding is a response to the attack you can see coming, not something you build up.
means.5: Guard stacks up to five and stays until something takes it. Enough to absorb one heavy attack or two light ones.
means.8: Loose. A player who guards for two turns can walk through almost anything on the third.
means.99: No cap in practice. Turtling becomes a strategy, which is why this is not the default.

default_consumable_stack_cap.question: How many of one Supplies consumable (Coffee, Tea, a Booster Dinner...) can you hold when its own Stack Cap cell in the Shop tab is blank?

means.3: Tight. Consumables are a small edge, not something to stockpile.
means.5: Cameron, 2026-09-27: every consumable without its own cap stops at five. Stops a player stacking twenty Coffees into one stage.
means.10: Loose. Enough to carry a stage well past its designed energy.

card_training_looks.question: In Rhetoric Training, how many cards can one draw show before the player has to learn the one in front of them?

means.1: No passing: the first card shown is the one you learn.
means.3: Cameron, 2026-09-27: the first card and two passes (the pop-up counts 1/3, 2/3, 3/3); the third must be learned.
means.5: Four passes. Close to picking whichever card you like.

ticker_speed_px_per_sec.question: How fast does the Office screen's news ticker scroll, in pixels per second?

means.50: Calm — every word is easy to read without rushing.
means.70: Cameron, 2026-09-28: between calm and a real ticker's brisk pace.
means.80: Brisker — reads like a real news ticker.
means.120: Fast — a glance, not a read.

ticker_pull_interval_seconds.question: How often does the ticker swap in a freshly-picked line?

means.8: Lines change quickly — more variety, less time to finish reading a longer one.
means.10: Cameron, 2026-09-28: a touch brisker than the original 12s default.
means.12: Enough time to read a line before the next one comes in.
means.20: Lines linger — fewer swaps, more time on each one.

funds_starting_cap.question: Before buying any Funds cap increase (SH19), how high can Funds actually go? sanban.json's own Funds max (1,000,000) is the absolute ceiling no amount of SH19 can ever push past — this is where a fresh run starts underneath it.

means.50000: Starts right at the Funds row's own starting value (50,000) — zero headroom until the first SH19 purchase.
means.100000: Cameron, 2026-10-04: one clean 100,000-yen tier above the 50,000 starting Funds. SH19's own 100,000-per-purchase increase then ratchets the cap up in nine more steps to the 1,000,000 ceiling.
means.200000: Generous early room — two tiers before the player has to think about the cap at all.
